adapter.source_necessity: a perfect-cuboid candidate on the q-fiber requires a rational point Q with c(Q) finite and nonzero and F3(Q) in (Q^*)^2
adapter.odd_numerator_valuation_obstruction: if some prime ell has v_ell(N(Q)) odd, then F3(Q) is not a rational square, hence Q cannot decode to a perfect-cuboid candidate on that source fiber
adapter.role_of_primitivity: primitivity is not needed for the single-point nonsquare implication; it is only a proposed global bookkeeping mechanism for forcing a new odd numerator valuation at every sufficiently large orbit index

torsion_scope.reason: Paper C's torsion-degeneracy lemma sends nonidentity torsion under c to 0 or a pole
torsion_scope.warning: a theorem only for N_n=Num(F3(nP)) does not automatically cover Num(F3(nP+T)) for every fixed torsion translate T

rank2_scope.warning: Paper C says an analogous two-variable input would be needed but does not define a two-variable primitive ordering/divisibility sequence

counterexample_to_naive_global_chain.conclusion: primitive divisor does not imply odd multiplicity
